# AutoPilot-rs

> AutoPilot-rs is a cross-platform, local-first task scheduler written in Rust. It runs shell tasks when configurable conditions (WiFi, Bluetooth, power, CPU/memory, processes, files, disks, screens, and others) are satisfied. It ships a CLI, an HTTP API, and a native GUI.

- [README](README.md): project overview, installation, quick start, configuration, and troubleshooting.

## Key source paths

- [CLI entry point](crates/autopilot-cli/src/main.rs): binary entry.
- [CLI commands](crates/autopilot-cli/src/cli): argument parsing, serve/stop/status/list/create/remove/gui.
- [HTTP routes](crates/autopilot-api/src/routes.rs): Axum routes and bind address.
- [API handlers](crates/autopilot-api/src/handlers): health, lifecycle, and job CRUD handlers.
- [Runtime facade](crates/autopilot-core/src/autopilot/mod.rs): `AutoPilot`, start/stop/reload, job loading.
- [Job model and runtime](crates/autopilot-core-job/src/job/mod.rs): job scheme, condition evaluation, task execution, status updates.
- [Conditions](crates/autopilot-core-conditions/src/conditions): condition implementations and schemas.
- [Task execution](crates/autopilot-core-task/src/task): shell command runner.
- [Schedules](crates/autopilot-core-time/src/time/mod.rs): `When` variants and cron expressions.
- [Configuration paths and storage](crates/autopilot-core-fs/src): config root, jobs directory, JSON/JSONC store.
- [Health checks](crates/autopilot-core-checks/src/checks.rs): API address, defaults, and `/health` client.

## Important facts

- Default API address: `http://127.0.0.1:7883`.
- Environment variables: `AUTOPILOT_HOST` (default `127.0.0.1`) and `AUTOPILOT_PORT` (default `7883`).
- `autopilot-rs serve` always starts the API; `--api` only suppresses automatic job start.
- The API is unauthenticated and uses plain HTTP. Keep it on loopback.
- API job CRUD writes files; `POST /reload` or `POST /restart` applies changes to the live runtime.
- Reload/restart failures currently return HTTP `200` with `"success": false`.
- Invalid job files are skipped by the loader; duplicate job IDs prevent the job set from loading.
- `file` condition `size_changed` currently checks a minimum size threshold; it does not detect a change from a previous size.
- A failed task is logged, but the job currently reports `Completed`.
- The Unix signal handler processes one `SIGHUP`; `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` exit directly.

## Development commands

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --locked
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo clippy -p autopilot-api --all-targets --locked
cargo run -p autopilot-rs -- --help
```

The workspace contains both `autopilot-rs` and `autopilot-gui`; always pass `-p autopilot-rs` when running the CLI with Cargo.
